To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

romantic autonomy is positively associated with romantic intimacy and friendship autonomy, that romantic autonomy is higher among girls than among boys, and that romantic autonomy is uniquely related to both maternal and friend intimacy and autonomy.
romantic autonomy is positively related to intimacy and affiliation in romantic relationships and that romantic autonomy is linked to both intimacy and autonomy in other relationships.

romantic autonomy in mid-adolescence is linked to romantic intimacy, but this link is stronger in shorter-term relationships; that it is also linked to intimacy and affiliation in mother-adolescent relationships and in adolescent-friend relationships; that it varies with age and gender, with girls being higher in romantic autonomy than boys; and that it is linked to intimacy and independence in both mother-adolescence and friend-adolescent dyads.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interpersonal context of adolescent romantic relationships.
the interconnection of romantic relationships, family relationships and friendship relationships.
the interpersonal context of autonomy in romantic relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study suggest that the interpersonal context of autonomy in adolescent romantic relationships is complex and multifaceted.
romantic autonomy in adolescents is linked to romantic intimacy, and that romantic autonomy is also linked to autonomy in both maternal relationships and friend relationships.
the results of this study highlight the interconnection of autonomy and intimacy within romantic relationships and the linkages across relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

romantic autonomy is an important aspect of romantic relationships in mid adolescence, and is related to both the intimacy of the relationship and the intimacy and autonomy of the mother-child and friend relationships.
the development of autonomy in romantic relationships is a complex process, involving the interplay of the individual, the partner, and the social context.
the more autonomy a person experiences in their romantic relationship the more they experience intimacy in that relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adolescents who are more autonomous in their romantic relationships tend to be more autonomous in other relationships, and this autonomy is associated with greater intimacy in those relationships.
romantic relationships are an important context for the development of adolescents’ sense of self.
romantic autonomy is not an isolated construct, but rather a relational one.
